sections.h2: Ways to sell a Gilbert house
sections.html:
Gilbert sellers have three doors to choose from: an agent, a do-it-yourself sale, or a buyer who pays cash and wants the house exactly as you leave it. Each door swaps time, effort and money in its own mix. Condition, deadline and tolerance for prep work should decide it.

  • With an agent: someone prepares, photographs and markets the house, and closing waits for the buyer's lender to finish its review.
  • On your own: pricing, showings, disclosures and negotiation all land on you.
  • Cash, as-is: good for inherited homes, postponed repairs, tenants already living there and owners racing a deadline.

At $575,100, the median owner-occupied home in Gilbert is far above the $332,700 national figure. Replacing a roof or an air conditioner costs serious money at those prices, which is why owners often put a repaired listing's net next to a direct as-is sale's net.

Gilbert is a town in Maricopa County, southeast of Phoenix, south of Mesa, northeast of Chandler and northwest of Queen Creek. It is larger than most Arizona cities despite its legal status as a town. The population is 287,285 as of July 1, 2025, up from 267,918 in 2020, across about 68.6 square miles.

Homeowners live in 73.1% of the houses. Rent is $2,110 at the median, household income is $122,551, and 96,363 households average 2.90 people. Commutes take 25.9 minutes on average. The Santan Freeway stretch of Loop 202 carries most traffic, and US 60 brushes the northern edge at the Higley Road interchange.

Gilbert Public Schools covers most addresses, though sections fall under Chandler Unified, Mesa Public Schools or Higley Unified. Look the district up by street address before you advertise it.

sections.h2: Permits and town rules before listing
sections.html:
For permit questions, reach the Town's Development Services office at (480) 503-6700 or onestopshop@gilbertaz.gov. Customer hours are extended for most services, from 7 a.m. until 6 p.m. Monday to Thursday, while building, engineering and fire inspections keep separate schedules.

Did you finish a patio, pool, garage conversion or accessory dwelling without pulling a permit? Ask Development Services what record exists before you commit to a contract. The permit page lists a residential fee calculator, an accessory dwelling unit guide, pool fence rules, a noise ordinance and a permit extension request form, and each one speaks to something an inspector is likely to ask. An HOA's covenants may restrict exterior changes, so pull those papers early.

Nightly rentals in Gilbert need a Town license, approved by the Council in June 2023. The license and renewal fee is $250 as of October 1, 2026. Under A.R.S. 9-500.39 the state keeps a town from banning them, but a permit, emergency contact details and liability coverage can be required. Send licensing questions to ShortTermRentals@gilbertaz.gov.

If tenants live there, A.R.S. 33-1902 requires you to maintain a registration with the county assessor and refresh it within ten days of a change. Review it before listing.

sections.h2: Deed recording and the affidavit of value
sections.html:
The deed goes to the Maricopa County Recorder with an affidavit of value attached. Without it the deed comes back, unless an exemption is written on its face (A.R.S. 11-1133). Buyer and seller sign it side by side. The form covers parcel number, sale date, price and financing, and adds two questions: is personal property 5% or more of the price, and will the buyer live there or rent?

Under A.R.S. 11-1134, these transfers can skip the affidavit if the deed cites the exemption:

  • Gifts
  • Court-ordered conveyances
  • Nominal-consideration transfers inside the family circle (spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, siblings)
  • Corrective deeds repeating one already recorded

Filing costs $30 an instrument (A.R.S. 11-475), and that number swallows the $2 transfer fee in A.R.S. 11-1132. The office at 602-506-3535 answers general questions but will not coach you through forms. For the documents themselves, rely on a title company or attorney. A cash buyer's deal travels the same escrow and title road as a listed sale.

Two payments make up a Gilbert tax year, both billed by Maricopa County. A.R.S. 42-18052 fixes the late dates.

BillPayableLate after
First halfOctober 15:00 p.m., November 1
Second halfMarch 15:00 p.m., May 1
Total of $100 or lessOctober 1After December 31

A weekend November 1 pushes the first-half date, as the county calendar shows. The escrow officer splits the year's tax between you and the buyer at closing. Ask how, and make sure no half is left owing.

Challenging the Assessor's number is possible, though the calendar is tight. Between January 1 and March 1 the Notice of Value arrives. Sixty days from its mailing date is your window for the petition for review, and the Assessor replies by August 15. A refusal leaves 25 days to appeal to the State Board of Equalization. A lawsuit must be filed by December 15 of the notice year or within 60 days of the last administrative ruling.

Know the limit before you spend effort. Only full cash value can be contested, and your bill rests on the limited property value, which generally cannot grow faster than 5% a year.

sections.h2: What Gilbert buyers tend to ask
sections.html:
Buyers in a town this size arrive with a short list. Which school district is the address in? How far is the freeway on-ramp, and what does the drive to Phoenix look like at rush hour? Is there an HOA, and will its rules block a pool fence or a casita? Can guests stay by the night, or does the owner need a Town license first?

You win time by answering before you are asked. Print the district name, note the nearest Loop 202 interchange, attach the HOA covenants and state plainly if the house has been rented out. A listing sheet that answers these questions reads as an organized seller, and an organized seller gets fewer low offers built on fear of the unknown. The same sheet helps a cash buyer move faster, since fewer surprises means a quicker yes.

Price talk is the other half of it. With values this high, a buyer's agent will lean on any visible repair to argue for a discount, so a fresh coat of paint on weathered trim or a serviced air conditioner can pay for itself. If you would rather not do repair work at all, that is a legitimate reason to look at an as-is sale, where the buyer carries the work and you carry nothing but the paperwork.

Assemble a sale folder holding the parcel number, newest tax bill, HOA contact, repair list and permit records. Whoever opens it should be able to price the house quickly. If the house is vacant, inherited or tenant-occupied, say so up front, since closing mechanics change.

Want speed? Ask for a written offer stating the closing date and your take-home amount, then compare it with a listing price once repairs, agent fees, carrying costs and slow weeks are deducted. Read the whole agreement before signing, ideally after a title company or attorney has.

The title company retires your mortgage and any liens at the table, records the deed with the county and pays you the remainder. Bring photo identification. Ask ahead of time whether keys, garage openers and HOA fobs should change hands that day.

faqs.q: Do I need an affidavit of value to sell a house in Gilbert?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the transfer is exempt. A.R.S. 11-1133 requires buyer and seller to sign an affidavit that goes with the deed, and the Maricopa County Recorder refuses a deed without it unless an exemption such as a gift or a court-ordered conveyance is noted on the deed.

faqs.q: When are Gilbert property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due October 1 and half is due March 1. The first half turns delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second half after 5:00 p.m. on May 1, except that bills of $100 or less are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31.

Yes, with a Town license. Arizona law prevents a town from prohibiting short-term rentals, and Gilbert requires a license under its June 2023 ordinance. The license and renewal fee is $250 as of October 1, 2026, and ShortTermRentals@gilbertaz.gov handles questions.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Gilbert home's value?
faqs.a: You have 60 days from the date the Maricopa County Assessor mailed the Notice of Value. The petition goes to the Assessor first, and a denial can be taken to the State Board of Equalization within 25 days or to court by December 15.

faqs.q: Who records the deed after a Gilbert sale?
faqs.a: The Maricopa County Recorder records it, usually through the title or escrow company handling the closing. Recording is $30 per instrument, including the $2 transfer fee, and the office can be reached at 602-506-3535 for general questions.
